1 صَمِعَتِ الأُذُنُ , aor.
صَمَعَ , inf. n. صَمَعٌ, (Msb, TA,) The ear was [small: (see أَصْمَعُ:) or] cleaving [to the head], and small: (Msb:) or was small, and not pointed, or tapering, or slender at the extremity, and had a contraction in the middle, and a cleaving to the head: or clave to the side of the face, from its base, and was short, not pointed, or tapering, or slender at the extremity: or was narrow, or contracted, in its hole, and pointed. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
